text:
anya: Heads up — noticed sustained egress pressure out of eu-west-2 around 02:10 UTC, lots of short-lived spikes that correlate with a jump in GPU tail latency. not an OOM, looks like network queuing.

infra-bot: alert: egress-saturation eu-west-2 (02:11 UTC) — 95th p99 egress throughput above 85% of NIC capacity for 4m, impacted pods: 14, increased retry rate on inference gateway. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/egress/eu-west-2

matt: thanks, anya. are the affected tenants on shared pools or dedicated?

anya: mixed. 9 on shared hetero-silo, 5 on small dedicated pools (d-1/d-2) that share the same top-of-rack egress link.

kevin: that matches a noisy-neighbor pattern where a dedicated pool sits behind the same ToR as a heavy-egress tenant on shared. we've seen TCP buffer bloat causing per-token latency to spike.

lucy: cost question — if we start routing away to other AZs or spin up spare NIC capacity, what's the expected monthly delta for a 2h mitigation window?

matt: rough ballpark: cross-AZ egress + reserved burst will be ~0.6-0.9k USD per hour for eu-west. spinning ephemeral nodes is cheaper but slo hit if we don't do prefix caching.

kevin: proposal: implement per-tenant egress circuit-breaker at the sidecar level — when tenant egress > X MiB/s over 1m, mark as "egress-throttled" and route new requests to fallback routing policy (lower-cost variant / dedicated fallback pool / degrade to smaller model).

anya: +1 on circuit-breaker concept. want to avoid full offline evictions, prefer graceful degrade and automatic recovery.

dinesh: i can prototype a rate-limit + token-bucket sidecar config today. simple k8s patch we tested in staging looks like this:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: egress-throttle-config
data:
  bucket_rate: "80MiB/s"
  window_sec: "60"
  action: "route-fallback"
```
This will emit metrics to /metrics and a span when a tenant crosses threshold.

kevin: for routing we should tie the fallback to a routing policy that prefers dedicated pools in other racks first, then shared pools in same region, then cross-AZ as a last resort. avoids surprise egress charges.

matt: agree. also add an early detection probe that looks at NIC queue length and conn_handshake_retries to trigger a soft backoff before the breaker trips.

lucy: we need a quick cost/impact matrix before pushing prod changes. can dinesh add expected saved token cost per mitigation and worst-case cross-AZ egress cost?

dinesh: will add numbers. initial conservative estimate: if breaker avoids a fallback to cross-AZ for 20 tenants for 2h each, saves ~12k tokens worth of compute + avoids ~1.2k USD egress. will confirm.

anya: plan suggestion: 1) deploy sidecar throttle config as a canary in eu-west-2 on 1 rack (20 pods) 2) enable routing policy that routes "egress-throttled" to fallback pool w/ 1% canary traffic 3) monitor p99 latency, retries, and cost for 2h window 4) rollback if error rate > 2% or p99 > baseline + 30ms.

kevin: i can own the routing policy PR. will prepare patch for router table TTLs to ensure quick failback.

matt: i'll add the soft-probe script and a prometheus alert for early NIC queue growth.

lucy: i'll run the cost sim and confirm finance OK for a short surge window.

infra-bot: link: incident timeline & current traces https://internal.redwood/trace/1815000000

anya: owners: kevin (routing), dinesh (sidecar), matt (probe/alert), lucy (cost), anya (coord). target: canary deploy in next 3h.

kevin: starting PR now, will tag owners and post link when ready.

matt: deploying probe to canary rack in 15. will report back with first 30m metrics.

anya: thanks all. quick note — prioritize graceful fallback not outright blocking. want apps to stay online. :thumbsup:

lucy: once we have canary numbers, i'll prepare a blameless summary for CS so they can tell affected customers what happened and what we did.

anya: ok closing thread for now, will update once canary finishes.
